extracted.intended_audience: depositors of microorganisms for patent purposes; international depositary authorities (IDAs); industrial property offices; third parties requesting samples
extracted.subtask_short: Budapest Treaty deposit and sample rules
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and legal requirements under the Budapest Treaty for making original and new deposits of microorganisms, transfer of deposits between IDAs, and the procedures/conditions for furnishing samples to entitled parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When a time period is expressed as a certain number of months, computation starts on the day following the relevant event and the period expires in the subsequent month on the day with the same number; if that month has no such day, the period expires on the last day of that month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: notification received January 15 → new deposit due by April 15; notification January 31 → due by April 30. The same formula applies mutatis mutandis for time periods in years (Rule 12bis.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑month limit for making a new deposit (start date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-month time limit for making a new deposit begins when the depositor receives notification from the IDA of its inability to furnish samples, except where the IDA has ceased to function or lost its status and has not notified the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IDA has not notified the depositor within six months of the International Bureau's publication of its loss of status, Article 4(1)(e) provides that the three‑month period starts from that publication date; in practice Contracting States should ensure transfer of deposits so Article 4(1)(e) should not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and viability testing on new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Having received and accepted a new deposit, the IDA must test its viability and issue to the depositor a receipt and a viability statement (the latter identical to that for an original deposit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receipt must be made out on international form BP/5 and contain indications analogous to an original deposit receipt, but referring to a 'new deposit'. It must include particular items (see additional receipt content criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt content for new deposit (mandatory particulars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 7.4 requires that the receipt for a new deposit include, in addition to standard receipt items, (vi) an indication of the relevant reason and relevant date as stated by the depositor (per Rule 6.2(a)(ii)); (vii) where Rule 6.2(a)(iii) applies, a reference to any scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation indicated by the depositor; and (viii) the accession number given to the previous deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new deposit is with another IDA, the accession number may or may not change; when issuing a receipt the IDA must also send copies of the new receipt and the last positive viability statement issued for the previous deposit to the depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of original date of deposit (requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To retain the original date of deposit, a viable sample of the newly deposited microorganism must be received by the IDA no later than the last day of the three‑month time limit under Article 4(1)(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a viable sample is received later, the earliest date of deposit that can be applied is the actual receipt date. Loss of the original deposit date can have serious patent implications; timely action is as important as for original deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act promptly on IDA notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving notification from the IDA that it can no longer furnish samples, the depositor should immediately note the date and calculate the deadline for any new deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is emphasized: last‑minute new deposits carry the same risks as last‑minute original deposits (see paragraphs 43–49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain possibility of transfer before making new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IDA is unable to furnish samples because of loss of status or discontinuance of function, the depositor should ascertain whether his deposited microorganisms will be transferred to another IDA under Rule 5.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transfer will occur, the right to make a new deposit under Article 4 does not exist (Article 4(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a different IDA for a new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If making a new deposit with another IDA, the depositor must ensure the chosen IDA will accept the microorganism and determine its administrative and technical requirements, since they may differ from the original IDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right to make a new deposit in another IDA exists only in cases of discontinuance or loss of status (Article 4(1)(b)(i)) or export/import restrictions (Article 4(1)(b)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure identity of the microorganism in new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositor must take care to ensure the microorganism submitted as a new deposit is the same as that previously deposited, since his allegation under Article 4(1)(c) can be contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make careful checks and keep supporting documentation to avoid disputes about identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement to accompany a new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositor should append a signed statement giving the reason for making a new deposit, the date on which he received notification from the IDA of its inability to furnish samples, and a declaration that the microorganism is the same as previously deposited (Article 4(1)(c) and Rule 6.2(a)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many IDAs use WIPO model forms BP/2 and BP/3 for new deposits; if these are used, a separate statement is unnecessary. Ensure forms include required indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional documentation for new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with forms and the declaration, the depositor must submit (a) a copy of the receipt for the previous deposit, (b) a copy of the latest positive viability statement for the previous deposit, and (c) if applicable, the latest scientific description/taxonomic designation sent for the previous deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supporting documents help link the new deposit to the previous one and support retention of original deposit date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for transfer of deposits between IDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits may be transferred when the IDA ceases or temporarily suspends functions; when assurances leading to IDA status are withdrawn; when an IDA fails to meet Treaty/Regulations obligations and status is limited or terminated; or when the furnishing State/organization ceases to be a party or recognize the Treaty (various Articles/Rules cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer may apply to all or certain kinds of deposited microorganisms; reasons other than absolute termination can be partial in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of Contracting State on transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting State or intergovernmental industrial property organization that furnished assurances (Article 6(1)) must ensure prompt transfer of affected deposits and relevant files to another IDA and, as far as possible, ensure the defaulting IDA notifies affected depositors (Rule 5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State or organization decides the substitute IDA, but the depositor may request additional transfers at his own expense (Rule 5.1(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of substitute IDA on transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute IDA must issue a receipt (international form BP/6) for transferred microorganisms, test viability and issue a viability statement; the BP/6 receipt must include specified particulars (i)–(viii) per Rule 7.5 (name/address of IDA and depositor, date of transfer, identification reference, accession numbers, prior IDA details, references to scientific description/designation where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The viability statement is identical to that for original/new deposits; the receipt contents are governed strictly by Rule 7.5 and must record transfer provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor's responsibilities after transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the depositor has minimal active participation in transfer, he should be aware he may need to notify new accession numbers to industrial property offices with applications referring to the original deposit, and should ascertain whether his deposit will be transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because transfer is not absolutely guaranteed ('to the fullest extent possible' under Rule 5.1), the depositor should exercise his right to make new deposits if transfer will not occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle for furnishing samples (entitlement verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs are not expected to judge entitlement under the patent laws of every country; therefore an IDA will furnish a sample only if the request is accompanied by depositor's written authorization, a certificate from a competent industrial property office indicating legitimacy, or where a competent industrial property office has notified the IDA that distribution is allowed (Rule 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11 recognizes three situations: requests from interested industrial property offices (11.1), requests with depositor authorization (11.2), and requests from parties legally entitled (11.3). IDAs generally refuse requests not compliant with these mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests from interested industrial property offices (content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial property office requesting a sample must accompany the request with a declaration that (i) an application referring to the deposit has been filed and the subject matter involves the microorganism or its use; (ii) that application is pending or has led to grant of a patent; (iii) the sample is needed for the purposes of a patent procedure effective in that Contracting State/organization; (iv) the sample and information will be used only for that patent procedure (Rule 11.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions define an 'interested' office and prohibit use of samples for purposes other than the stated patent procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests with the depositor's authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 11.2 an IDA shall furnish a sample to (i) the depositor on request, and (ii) any authority, natural person or legal entity on the request of such party provided the request is accompanied by a declaration of the depositor authorizing the furnishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes depositor's right to obtain and to authorize distribution of his deposit; however, the depositor cannot prevent furnishing to parties legally entitled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests from parties legally entitled — industrial office certification (Rule 11.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDA shall furnish a sample to a 'certified party' upon a request on an Assembly-fixed form where the industrial property office certifies (i) an application referring to the deposit has been filed and involves the microorganism/use; (ii) publication for patent purposes has been effected (except where special phrase applies); (iii) that the certified party has a right to a sample under the law governing patent procedure before that office and that required conditions (if any) have been fulfilled, or where entitlement exists prior to publication the office must cite the legal provision (Rule 11.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects depositors and IDAs from illegal furnishing by requiring certification of entitlement and of the office's competence to certify; for PCT international applications the office may certify international publication or its own publication (Rule 11.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative mechanism — accession number lists (Rule 11.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property offices may, in respect of patents granted and published by them, communicate to any IDA lists of accession numbers given to deposits cited in those patents; the IDA shall, on request of any party, furnish a sample where the accession number has been so communicated, and certification under 11.3(a) is not required for those accession numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows countries whose laws make organisms freely available after grant to bypass certification; in practice few offices provide such notification and IDAs are often left to ascertain patent issuance themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, formality and signature requirements for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications under Rules 11.1, 11.2, 11.3 must be in writing, signed and dated. Language requirements depend on the official language(s) of the IDA and may be English, French, Russian or Spanish, with the International Bureau providing certified translations where needed (Rule 11.4(a),(b),(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the official language of the IDA is Russian or Spanish, communications may still be in English or French and the IB will translate free of charge; conversely, requests from offices in Russian/Spanish can be translated to English/French by the IB on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of requests (Rule 11.4(d)/(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests under Rules 11.1, 11.2 or 11.3(a) must contain: (i) name and address of the industrial property office/authorized/certified party; (ii) the accession number; (iii) for Rule 11.1 the date and number of the application/patent referring to the deposit; (iv) for Rule 11.3(a) the indications in (iii) and the name/address of the certifying industrial property office. For Rule 11.3(b) only the requesting party's name/address and accession number are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests not on the appropriate form or without the required endorsement are automatically refused except where Rules 11.1, 11.2 or 11.3(b) apply; some offices may require additional forms to satisfy national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indications accompanying furnished samples (marking and documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The container sent shall be marked by the IDA with the accession number and accompanied by a copy of the receipt (Rule 7), an indication of any properties dangerous to health or the environment, and, upon request, an indication of the conditions the IDA uses for cultivation and storage of the microorganism (Rule 11.4(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are standard precautions; the receipt copy requirement is emphasized as a Treaty provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to depositor when samples furnished to others
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IDA furnishes a sample to any interested party other than the depositor, it shall promptly notify the depositor in writing of that fact, the date of furnishing, and the name and address of the party/office to whom it was furnished, accompanied by a copy of the pertinent request and declarations/forms (Rule 11.4(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors may waive their right to be informed (many do) and IDAs commonly comply; some IDAs charge lower storage fees if the depositor waives notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for furnishing samples and descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA may charge a fee for furnishing samples in all cases except where the recipient is an industrial property office, which must be supplied free of charge (Rule 11.4(h) and Rule 12.1(a)(iv)). Parties entitled to a copy of the most recent scientific description/taxonomic designation may be charged a fee (Rule 7.6 and Rule 12.1(a)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees charged by an IDA cannot be varied according to the nationality or residence of the party paying (Rule 12.1(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical routes for requesting a sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where Rule 11.3(b) applies, a simple requester should expect the IDA to ask him to (a) obtain depositor authorization (Rule 11.2(ii)), (b) obtain certification from the appropriate industrial property office (Rule 11.3(a)), or (c) provide evidence of issuance of a US patent (because US patents generally require organism availability after grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subsection translates Treaty requirements into practical steps for third parties. Choice of route depends on knowledge of depositor identity and where patent applications were filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for obtaining sample with depositor authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The requesting party should obtain a written, dated, signed declaration from the depositor authorizing the IDA to furnish a sample (form BP/11 can be used but is not essential), then send this declaration with his request and purchase order to the IDA (Rule 11.2(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11.2 presupposes knowledge of the depositor's identity; IDAs will not normally divulge depositor identity (Rule 9.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for obtaining sample with industrial office certification (BP/12)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under Rule 11.3(a) must be made on a form corresponding to BP/12 (or office equivalent). The requester should (a) ask the competent industrial property office or the IDA for the form, (b) complete the part for the requesting party, and (c) send the entire form to the industrial property office with any fee payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices combine BP/12 with other national forms (e.g., EPO combining with Rule 33 EPC requirements). IDAs may supply BP/12 but may not know which offices are competent to certify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining samples cited in US patents (evidence requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because US practice generally makes microorganisms referred to in a published/granted US patent freely available after grant, a requester should provide the patent number/date, name(s) of applicant(s) and a copy of the page referring to the accession number as evidence if the IDA is not aware of the publication (paragraphs 104–105).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester cannot supply such evidence, furnishing may be delayed until the IDA verifies publication; not all IDAs verify publication proactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining samples under Rule 11.3(b) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a sample where an industrial property office has communicated accession numbers under Rule 11.3(b), a requesting party only needs to give his name and address and quote the accession number (some IDAs request WIPO model form BP/13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because few offices supply such lists, this route is infrequently applicable in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health, safety, and national import/quarantine requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures under the Budapest Treaty relate only to right to receive samples; they do not override any requirements such as import/quarantine regulations, health and safety procedures, plant disease regulations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must obtain any permits or licenses and comply with safety requirements necessary for handling the organism in question before receiving a sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists of IDAs and kinds of microorganisms accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide provides a current list of international depositary authorities (IDAs) by country and lists the kinds of microorganisms each IDA accepts (subject to change; consult WIPO site for up-to-date information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lists in the Guide are for information only; up-to-date acceptance lists and fee information are available on the Budapest Treaty website (Rule 13.2(a) reference).
